Summary: In the current release (SCOPe 2.08, periodic update 2.08-2026-08-16) all three structures sit in the same lineage: class a (all-alpha) > fold a.47 "STAT-like" (sunid 47654; fold comment: "4 long helices; bundle, left-handed twist (coiled coil); right-handed superhelix") > superfamily a.47.2 "t-snare proteins" (47661) > family a.47.2.1 "t-snare proteins" (47662). But SCOPe now treats the two kinds of entries very differently, and that difference is the point: the fragment entries carry an explicit incompleteness flag, while 1dn1 chain B has been demoted from a curated domain to an "automated match" that inherits its classification from the revised structure 3c98.

1. The fragments 1br0 and 1ez3 are flagged as incomplete representatives of the fold, not as evidence for it.
- d1br0a_ (sunid 17772; NMR, 120 residues, rat syntaxin-1A Habc region) and d1ez3a_/b_/c_ (sunids 17768-17770; crystal, 124 residues) are classified under protein "Syntaxin 1A N-terminal domain" (47663), species Norway rat [TaxId 10116] (47664).
- Each carries the curator comment "three-helical fragment; similar to one spectrin repeat" (present already in SCOP 1.75, where 1br0 also carried "mutant").
- New in SCOPe 2.08 relative to 1.75: each fragment domain has a structured inconsistency record, abbreviation "ms": "missing some secondary structures that made up less than one-third of the common domain" (scope: domain, not inherited). In 1.75 the annotations endpoint shows comments only and no inconsistency.
- Biological interpretation: the a.47 fold is defined by four long helices; the Habc fragment is a three-helix bundle. So the fold (and superfamily/family) label on d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_ is inherited from the curated protein node because the sequence is syntaxin-1A, not because the fragment itself displays the STAT-like fold. Fragment-based fold assignments in SCOP(e) are statements about the parent protein's domain, and the "ms" flag is the machine-readable warning that structural comparison against this domain will only cover part of the common core. The "similar to one spectrin repeat" comment is a further caution: a three-helix bundle resembles the spectrin repeat (fold a.7) at the fold/analogy level only; that resemblance is not homology, and family a.47.2.1 membership rests on syntaxin sequence identity, not on the spectrin-like shape. These fragments should therefore not be used as templates for the full STAT-like four-helix fold, and ASTRAL-style representative selection should prefer a complete domain over them.

2. 1dn1 chain B is no longer the curated "full domain"; it is an automated match to the revised entry 3c98.
- 1dn1 (nSec1/Munc18a-syntaxin-1A complex) was obsoleted on 2008-03-25 and replaced by 3c98 ("Revised structure of the munc18a-syntaxin1 complex"). SCOPe 2.08 still lists 1dn1 as classified_in_release, but its history changed: in SCOP 1.75 d1dn1b_ was a manually curated domain (sunid 17771) under the same protein/species nodes as 1br0 and 1ez3; it is absent from SCOPe 2.01 through 2.05 (1dn1 shows classified_in_release=false in 2.05); it re-entered in 2.06 as a new domain (sunid 302344) and remains so in 2.07 and 2.08.
- In 2.08 d1dn1b_ hangs under protein "automated matches" (191190; node comment "not a true protein") and species "Rattus norvegicus" (311131, no TaxId), with domain comment "automated match to d3c98b_". It has no inconsistency flags because the automated pipeline does not evaluate completeness; its homology scope is simply the domain-level (px) placement.
- The curated representative of the complete rat syntaxin-1A N-terminal domain is now d3c98b_ (sunid 173092), which sits under the original protein node 47663/species 47664 alongside the fragments. The chain-level hits endpoint for 1dn1B confirms 3c98B is its cluster representative (100% identity over all 267 residues of 1dn1B; 95.7% coverage of 3c98B).
- Important boundary caveat: "full domain" overstates what 1dn1 B and 3c98 B contain. Both are classified as one whole-chain a.47.2.1 domain (222 and 247 residues) whose sequence includes the Habc helices, the linker, and the H3 SNARE-motif helix held in the closed conformation by Munc18. In SNARE complexes the H3 motif is classified separately in class h (coiled coil, SNARE fusion complex, h.1.2). So the Habc domain proper is captured completely by neither set: the fragments are pure Habc but short of the fold definition, and the complex chains are complete Habc plus an extra non-Habc helix lumped into the domain by whole-chain assignment.

3. What this changes for interpretation and use.
- Fold-level claims from fragments: treat d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_ as homology-inherited labels with a documented "ms" deficiency. Do not infer that the Habc fragment independently adopts the four-helix STAT-like fold, and do not use fold-level similarity to spectrin repeats as evidence of common ancestry; homology in SCOPe is asserted only at superfamily and below (here family a.47.2.1 implies common ancestry with Sso1, Vam3p N-terminal domain, syntaxin 6/SNAP-25 homolog, and Vti1-like 2 N-terminal domains).
- Template and representative choice: use d3c98b_ (or 3c98 chain B coordinates) rather than 1dn1 for a complete, curated syntaxin-1A N-terminal domain; 1dn1 is obsolete, was revised, and its SCOPe domain is only an automated sequence match. The fragments remain useful for the isolated Habc bundle but will be deprioritized by representative-selection criteria that penalize inconsistencies and incomplete domains.
- Function transfer: Munc18 binding of the closed conformation requires the H3 motif present only in 1dn1/3c98 chain B, so SNARE-regulatory function cannot be transferred from the Habc fragments merely because they share the a.47.2.1 label; conversely, class e placement of the Munc18 partner (d1dn1a_, d3c98a_ in e.25.1.1) reflects a multi-domain whole-chain assignment, not a single fold.
- Required external evidence: SCOPe's comments do not say which helix is missing or where the Habc/H3 boundary lies. Confirming that the fragments lack the fourth helix, and delimiting Habc from H3 in 3c98 B, requires inspection of the coordinates or DSSP secondary structure, and structural superposition (e.g., FATCAT) against other a.47 members; the FATCAT chain-statistics endpoint is not applicable at the domain level for d1dn1b_.

Fragment-based fold assignments in SCOP(e) are statements about the parent protein's domain, and the "ms" flag is the machine-readable warning that structural comparison against this domain will only cover part of the common core. The "similar to one spectrin repeat" comment is a further caution: a three-helix bundle resembles the spectrin repeat (fold a.7) at the fold/analogy level only; that resemblance is not homology, and family a.47.2.1 membership rests on syntaxin sequence identity, not on the spectrin-like shape. These fragments should therefore not be used as templates for the full STAT-like four-helix fold, and ASTRAL-style representative selection should prefer a complete domain over them.

2. 1dn1 chain B is no longer the curated "full domain"; it is an automated match to the revised entry 3c98.
- 1dn1 (nSec1/Munc18a-syntaxin-1A complex) was obsoleted on 2008-03-25 and replaced by 3c98 ("Revised structure of the munc18a-syntaxin1 complex"). SCOPe 2.08 still lists 1dn1 as classified_in_release, but its history changed: in SCOP 1.75 d1dn1b_ was a manually curated domain (sunid 17771) under the same protein/species nodes as 1br0 and 1ez3; it is absent from SCOPe 2.01 through 2.05 (1dn1 shows classified_in_release=false in 2.05); it re-entered in 2.06 as a new domain (sunid 302344) and remains so in 2.07 and 2.08.
- In 2.08 d1dn1b_ hangs under protein "automated matches" (191190; node comment "not a true protein") and species "Rattus norvegicus" (311131, no TaxId), with domain comment "automated match to d3c98b_". It has no inconsistency flags because the automated pipeline does not evaluate completeness; its homology scope is simply the domain-level (px) placement.
- The curated representative of the complete rat syntaxin-1A N-terminal domain is now d3c98b_ (sunid 173092), which sits under the original protein node 47663/species 47664 alongside the fragments. The chain-level hits endpoint for 1dn1B confirms 3c98B is its cluster representative (100% identity over all 267 residues of 1dn1B; 95.7% coverage of 3c98B).
- Important boundary caveat: "full domain" overstates what 1dn1 B and 3c98 B contain. Both are classified as one whole-chain a.47.2.1 domain (222 and 247 residues) whose sequence includes the Habc helices, the linker, and the H3 SNARE-motif helix held in the closed conformation by Munc18. In SNARE complexes the H3 motif is classified separately in class h (coiled coil, SNARE fusion complex, h.1.2). So the Habc domain proper is captured completely by neither set: the fragments are pure Habc but short of the fold definition, and the complex chains are complete Habc plus an extra non-Habc helix lumped into the domain by whole-chain assignment.

3. What this changes for interpretation and use.
- Fold-level claims from fragments: treat d1br0a_ and d1ez3a_ as homology-inherited labels with a documented "ms" deficiency. Do not infer that the Habc fragment independently adopts the four-helix STAT-like fold, and do not use fold-level similarity to spectrin repeats as evidence of common ancestry; homology in SCOPe is asserted only at superfamily and below (here family a.47.2.1 implies common ancestry with Sso1, Vam3p N-terminal domain, syntaxin 6/SNAP-25 homolog, and Vti1-like 2 N-terminal domains).
- Template and representative choice: use d3c98b_ (or 3c98 chain B coordinates) rather than 1dn1 for a complete, curated syntaxin-1A N-terminal domain; 1dn1 is obsolete, was revised, and its SCOPe domain is only an automated sequence match. The fragments remain useful for the isolated Habc bundle but will be deprioritized by representative-selection criteria that penalize inconsistencies and incomplete domains.
- Function transfer: Munc18 binding of the closed conformation requires the H3 motif present only in 1dn1/3c98 chain B, so SNARE-regulatory function cannot be transferred from the Habc fragments merely because they share the a.47.2.1 label; conversely, class e placement of the Munc18 partner (d1dn1a_, d3c98a_ in e.25.1.1) reflects a multi-domain whole-chain assignment, not a single fold.
- Required external evidence: SCOPe's comments do not say which helix is missing or where the Habc/H3 boundary lies. Confirming that the fragments lack the fourth helix, and delimiting Habc from H3 in 3c98 B, requires inspection of the coordinates or DSSP secondary structure, and structural superposition (e.g., FATCAT) against other a.47 members; the FATCAT chain-statistics endpoint is not applicable at the domain level for d1dn1b_.
